why-go-and-your-first-program.r: A team needed a small tool that ran on any server with no runtime installed. Go produced one static binary they could copy anywhere, which made rollout simple.
why-go-and-your-first-program.x: Go trades expressiveness for simplicity and fast builds. It suits network tools and services; be honest about where another language fits better, and about what the standard library already gives you.

types-structs-slices-and-maps.r: A function appended to a slice and the caller did not see the change, because the slice header was passed by value. Understanding how slices share arrays explained both the bug and the fix.
types-structs-slices-and-maps.x: Know zero values, slice capacity, aliasing and that maps are not safe for concurrent writes. These facts cause most early Go bugs and many production ones.

functions-errors-and-defer.r: An error was ignored in a cleanup path and a file was left half written. Checking every error and wrapping it with context made the real cause visible in the logs.
functions-errors-and-defer.x: Errors are values and part of your API. Wrap with context, return early, use defer for cleanup and be careful about what defer captures and when it runs.

interfaces-and-packages.r: Code that talked to a real database directly was hard to test. Defining a small interface for what it needed allowed a simple fake in tests. The tests then ran in milliseconds, with no network or database needed.
interfaces-and-packages.x: Accept interfaces, return structs, and keep interfaces small and defined where they are used. Package boundaries are design decisions, so avoid cycles and giant utility packages.

goroutines-channels-and-sync.r: A service leaked goroutines that waited forever on a channel nobody closed, and memory slowly grew until it was restarted. Giving every goroutine a clear way to stop fixed the leak.
goroutines-channels-and-sync.x: Every goroutine needs an owner and an exit. Prefer simple designs, use the race detector in tests and be careful with shared state, unbounded fan-out and blocking sends.

context-timeouts-and-cancellation.r: When a client gave up, the server kept running an expensive query for another minute. Passing the request context to the database call cancelled the work as soon as the client left.
context-timeouts-and-cancellation.x: Context is how deadlines and cancellation travel. Pass it as the first parameter, respect it in every blocking call and set timeouts at every boundary, including shutdown.

http-services-and-json.r: A service had no timeouts on its HTTP server or client, and one slow client held connections until the process ran out. Setting read, write and idle timeouts protected it.
http-services-and-json.x: Production HTTP needs timeouts, limits on body size, health endpoints and graceful shutdown. Decode JSON strictly where possible and never trust input shape.

testing-benchmarks-and-tooling.r: A function looked fast but a benchmark showed it allocated heavily in a hot path. Reducing allocations cut latency noticeably, and the benchmark stayed to guard against regressions.
testing-benchmarks-and-tooling.x: Table-driven tests, the race detector and benchmarks give strong confidence cheaply. Measure before optimising and watch for benchmarks that the compiler optimises away.

building-containers-and-cli-tools.r: A Go service shipped in a tiny image with just the binary started in under a second and had almost nothing for an attacker to use. Debugging it needed an ephemeral debug container, which the team prepared in advance.
building-containers-and-cli-tools.x: Static binaries and small images are a strength with trade-offs: no shell for debugging, certificates and time zone data to include. Version your tools and embed build information.

debugging-go-programs.r: A service slowly used more memory. A heap profile showed a cache that never evicted, and a goroutine dump found the workers that were stuck. Profiling pointed directly at the code.
debugging-go-programs.x: Learn to read stack traces, goroutine dumps and profiles. Expose profiling safely, use the race detector, and reproduce under load before deciding on a cause.
